title: The Crab Derby, 2027
logline: The forty-third annual. The wall of flyers, thirty long, and at its end Gully's daughter — seventeen — pinning hers with the practiced reach of someone who no longer needs the crate. Wood's page draws the wall and her hand.

panels.composition: The shingle wall, thirty flyers along it now, weathered to new, and at the end a young woman of seventeen in her father's apron pinning the newest with one easy reach. The page is mostly wall: thirty Februaries in a row. The crate she used to stand on is under the counter, holding bait.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a long shingle wall pinned with a row of thirty weathered-to-new hand-lettered crab flyers, a seventeen-year-old young woman in an apron pinning the newest with an easy reach, an old wooden crate under a counter holding bait, no other words legible

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Thirty flyers. She doesn't need the crate.
